Good Tuesday afternoon. Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 584 words, a 2-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

⚡️ Breaking: Cornell suspended parties at fraternity houses for the rest of the academic year amid mounting outrage over the university's handling of sexual assault allegations. "These measures will provide time for a thorough review of fraternity life at Cornell to determine whether and how it can safely continue," President Michael Kotlikoff said in a letter to the campus. Get the latest.
 
 
1 big thing: Guilfoyle out after misconduct reports
 
Kimberly Guilfoyle in Athens last year. Photo: Aris Messinis/AFP via Getty Images

Kimberly Guilfoyle has resigned as U.S. ambassador to Greece, Axios' Rebecca Falconer and Josephine Walker report.

  • Her exit follows Wall Street Journal reporting that she used her political connections to seek financial favors and promote private business interests.

Guilfoyle has denied any wrongdoing.

  • New White House press secretary Katie Zacharia told reporters today: "She has been a wonderful asset to the team and we wish her well."

🤳 Guilfoyle wrote on X: "My gratitude and respect for President Trump and Secretary [of State Marco] Rubio remain unwavering."

  • "I am proud of what we accomplished together, and I will always be a loyal supporter of President Trump and his mission to Make America Great Again."
White House press secretary Katie Zacharia conducts her debut briefing today. Photo: Kevin Lamarque/Reuters

📰 The Wall Street Journal reported last week that Guilfoyle allegedly sought $100,000 from a Trump donor to pay a credit card bill, and offered access to Trump administration officials in return.

  • Guilfoyle's lawyer disputed the authenticity of messages quoted by the Journal.
  • The U.S. Embassy in Athens said she has followed State Department ethics and gift-reporting guidelines.

👀 What we're watching: The State Department's inspector general is reviewing the allegations involving Guilfoyle, AP reports, citing an unnamed U.S. official.

2. 🪐 Off-world driving record
 
Graphic: NASA

NASA's Perseverance rover set a record for distance traveled on another planet or moon, the space agency says.

  • The Mars rover hit 28.10 miles on Sunday, topping the Opportunity rover's previous record of 28.06 miles.

🧭 NASA credits the achievement to Perseverance's autonomous navigation system.

  • The agency says: "The rover images the terrain while rolling, builds a 3D map of hazards, and plots its course between waypoints selected by rover planners on Earth — a capability the team calls 'thinking while driving.'"
Perseverance took this image of its own tracks on Sunday. Photo: NASA/JPL-Caltech

🚀 Steven Lee, project manager of the Curiosity and Perseverance rovers at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, said: "The original mission called for no more than 12.4 miles of driving."

  • "We've blown well past that, and with all mobility systems fully operational and favorable extended-ground-life test results, we expect Perseverance to keep adding to this record for many years to come."

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
Fresh-food refrigerators in Névez, France, sit empty yesterday after cyberattacks targeting supermarket chains. Photo: Fred Tanneau/AFP via Getty Images
  1. 👾 French investigators are probing cyberattacks that disabled fridges and freezers at hundreds of stores nationwide. Finance Minister Roland Lescure told lawmakers: "It was a wake-up call for everyone." Go deeper.
  2. 🧑‍⚖️ The Supreme Court, siding with the Trump administration, agreed to hear arguments in a watchdog's lawsuit seeking public records about Elon Musk's DOGE. Go deeper.
  3. 🤖 Kroger is laying off 3,000 corporate employees over the next three years as the grocery chain ramps up AI use. Go deeper.
 
 
4. 🏎️ 1 for the road: F1 returns to Africa
 
This new F1 track is planned near the new Kigali International Airport in Rwanda. Rendering: F1

Formula 1 is headed back to Africa for the first time since 1993, with Rwanda hosting a race in "the early 2030s."

  • The African Grand Prix will have a 10-year contract and take place at a track southeast of Rwanda's capital, Kigali.

🏁 Rwandan President Paul Kagame said at a launch event that he hopes the F1 event will "pave the way for other races to be hosted on the continent."
